title: I made a free tool to help fix your AI Pixel Art
author: oms1005
selftext:
Hi there, I made an app called PixelAid. I hope it helps your workflows.

First of all, it's totally **FREE**. I'm not selling this. It's open source, it runs in your browser, but there are desktop versions too, and I even have a CLI and MCP support in case you do want to use it with your AI agents.

So it's not really an AI tool. This app does not generate new assets for you. There are better ways to do that if you're starting from scratch. There are no payments here, no tokens to use. I'm not going to ask you for any prompts. PixelAid is meant as a step 2. To take you from "well I already have all this AI pixel art but I can't use it in Godot/Unity/My Game" because it's bad and unusable. Pixelaid makes it usable.

But if you're using AI image gen for pixel art, you probably have ran into some of the issues I try to fix here. Everything from fake grids, color overbloat, bad animations, and more. It's an early version, I will make it better, but I hope it helps your game dev journeys even a little.

If you use it and like it, or hate it, or have issues with it, I'd love to hear about it. Otherwise, enjoy your day.

comments.body: This looks really great.  So awesome that you're contributing this to the community for free and open source.  You're a rare breed these days.

comments.author: massivebacon
comments.body: Looks pretty cool! Would be nice to compare outputs with other tools like https://jenissimo.itch.io/unfaker

replies.author: oms1005
replies.body: Totally. Unfaker is a tool I love as well. And I use most of the same "fixes" in PixelAid, too, so definitely some overlap. I try to make some of the controls more available (like specific resize ability, etc) but at its core, we share some common algorithms for sure. Unfake.js is great - another great free tool that I hope everyone uses.

replies.author: oms1005
replies.body: Sure thing, I’m a big fan of Astropulse’s work! As I mentioned, PixelAid doesn’t generate art from prompts, so RetroDiffusion is amazing especially if you’re starting from new assets.

comments.author: ChocolateNuggy
comments.body: Hey, what tool do you recommend the most to start with before giving it off to your tool? What did you personally get the best results with?

replies.author: oms1005
replies.body:
If you have the budget, I do think RetroDiffusion is the best place to start, it'll save you most of the effort of fixing pixel grids. My tool can still help export to game engines, resize, or if you want to change other stuff, but RD is pretty good at what it does.

Otherwise, from the big players, I think Gemini/Nano Banana is till the best at pixel art. I have experiences less mixels with them for simpler art. NB is still the best at creating a clean hero or clean background - I like OpenAI's new image gen, but it really complicates backgrounds and adds gradients all over the place!
